title: Public-university lecturers’ ASA strike over pay and conditions of service
location: Three public universities; January government meeting at Fourah Bay College, Freetown
scope: National university-sector labor campaign; work-stoppage extent and any public assembly are not quantified
organizer: Academic Staff Associations at the University of Sierra Leone, Njala University, and Ernest Bai Koroma University, as reported by Politico SL and SwitSalone
participants_original: No strike-member count or public protest attendance count in the opened reports. A separate claim that more than 40,000 students were affected does not represent demonstrator turnout.
threshold_50_evidence: Unresolved and not established: opened articles describe an industrial work stoppage and representative meetings, not a public protest gathering or attendee count.

timeline.summary: The ASA-USL primary statement dated 20 November 2020 reports a planned 23 November resumption; its 4 January 2021 primary statement says action resumed after a suspension through 31 December. A government agreement says associations agreed to resume classes 3 February, and Njala's Registrar says academic activities had commenced that day. This traces work stoppage and academic reopening only: exact campaign inception and any public assembly's start/end remain unknown. Reports also conflict over whether the January Vice President meeting occurred Jan 19 or Jan 20 by relative wording.

demands.summary: ASA sought salary adjustment and other employment conditions from government. The November statement specifies adjustment, subvention and arrears; the January statement repeats a net salary adjustment condition; the February government agreement records commitments on a 50% adjustment from April plus other matters.

location.summary: The Jan 19 government meeting was scheduled at Fourah Bay College, Freetown; the reports do not locate a public protest gathering.

participants.summary: No public-protest attendance is reported. The >40,000 figure in S002 describes affected students, and work stoppage or representative meetings do not establish crowd size.

state_accommodation.summary: Sources document an actual Vice President meeting with lecturer representatives and a government agreement followed by academic reopening; this supports accommodation as response, not complete victory. Reports conflict on the January meeting date.

monthly_ownership.summary: The ASA work stoppage was active before January and resumed Jan 4 after a December suspension; classes resumed Feb 3. The onset of any qualifying physical public gathering is not established, so no month owner is assigned to a protest episode.

state_response_other.summary: No article establishes arrests, beatings, dispersal, ignore, killings, or shootings in response to this strike; those fields remain unknown.

notes: Boundary/context record only. The ASA work stoppage and negotiations remain distinct from any public assembly: no physical protest, >=50 turnout, or exact onset/end is established. Primary ASA statements document Nov 2020 action and Jan 4 resumption after a December suspension; the government agreement and Njala Registrar notice document Feb 3 class resumption. Affected students and meeting representatives are not protest turnout. January meeting-date conflict remains.
open_questions: Was any qualifying public assembly held by lecturers or students during or around the January strike?
What were the campaign's precise initial onset and the beginning/end of any physical assembly?
Did students carry out the threatened protest before classes resumed on February 3?
Resolve the conflicting reported date of the January Vice President meeting from a contemporaneous record.
